sourceIssues.reason: Write zeta_C(s) = Z(|k|^(-s)) with Z(T) = P(T)/((1-T)(1-|k|T)) and P(1) = |Pic^0(C)(k)|. review.reason: The smooth projective cubic y^2+y=x^3 in characteristic 2 has inverse (x,y+1); no affine geometric point equals its inverse, so its geometric 2-torsion consists only of the identity, not 2 points. In general [2]=V∘F on a g-dimensional abelian variety, deg(F)=2^g and deg([2])=2^(2g), so there are at most 2^g geometric kernel points. The group-scheme length is not the number of geometric points. Only the upper bound is needed here. This verdict is confined to the specified public preprint versions. The published JAMS text was not collated, and the review job remains incomplete.

sourceIssues.locator: Taniguchi author copy dated 18 February 2017, §4, p.6, index-two case; independently collated with arXiv:1701.02458v1, p.6.
sourceIssues.printed: by genus theory, the 2-torsion in the class group of K is bounded by the 2-torsion in the class group of F multiplied by O(2^t) … we obtain a bound of O_ε(|Disc(K)|^{1/4+ε})
sourceIssues.correction: A verified sufficient replacement is Klüners–Wang, arXiv:2003.12161v2, Theorem 2.1: h_2(K) ≤ 4^{e-1} h_2(F)², where t counts all ramified places including infinite ones and e = max(t,1), not simply t. Use this in a strong induction on n = [K:Q] rather than with Brauer–Siegel. If m = [F:Q] = n/2 ≥ 3 and the lower-degree case of the theorem gives exponent 1/2 - 1/(2m) + η, then D_F² ≤ D_K and 4^{e-1} ≪_{n,η} D_K^η give exponent 1/2 - 1/n + O(η), which is stronger than the 1/2 - 1/(2n) + ε the theorem needs. For n = 4, quadratic genus theory for F gives D_K^ε directly. This replacement neither proves nor refutes the printed one-factor relative bound, and it reaches the theorem's exponent without the printed D_K^{1/4+ε} claim for this case.
sourceIssues.reason: The displayed one-factor estimate has no derivation or precise citation in either preprint, and it is not what genus theory delivers. Genus theory for a quadratic K/F is the ambiguous class number formula, which bounds the Gal(K/F)-invariant classes: |Cl(K)^G| = h_F 2^{t-1} / [E_F : E_F ∩ N K^×] ≤ h_F 2^{t-1}. Passing from those to the 2-torsion costs a second factor: on Cl(K)[2] the map c ↦ c·σ(c) lands in Cl(K)^G and has kernel Cl(K)[2]^G, so the standard route gives only |Cl(K)[2]| ≤ |Cl(K)^G|², and genus theory bounds neither Cl(K)[2]^G nor Cl(K)^G by O(2^t)·h_2(F). That missing step is the whole of the gap, and it is load-bearing here: it is exactly what lets the printed argument finish by applying Brauer–Siegel to F, since h_2(F) ≪_ε |Disc F|^{1/2+ε} ≤ |Disc K|^{1/4+ε}. With the squared estimate that route gives only |Disc K|^{1/2+ε}, which is the trivial bound. Klüners–Wang Theorem 2.1 and its proof give the squared estimate h_2(K) ≤ 4^{e-1}h_2(F)², with Remark 2.2 improving it when the base 2-rank is zero; no statement in the literature gives the one-factor form. A weaker known upper bound is not evidence that the printed bound is false, and none is claimed here: the finding is that the step is asserted without proof or citation, not that it is refuted.

review.reason: Confirmed as a gap reaching the proof, resolving the deferral left by the previous checkpoint of this job, which asked that the failing step be identified before a verdict was given. It is this. Genus theory for a quadratic extension is the ambiguous class number formula, and it bounds |Cl(K)^{Gal(K/F)}| by h_F·2^{t-1} — by the full class number of F, not by h_2(F). The passage from ambiguous classes to 2-torsion is where the printed sentence jumps: the natural map Cl(K)[2] → Cl(K)^G, c ↦ c·σ(c), has kernel Cl(K)[2]^G, which genus theory does not bound by O(2^t), so the standard argument yields a square and not the printed single factor. That is also why the gap matters rather than being cosmetic: the printed one-factor form is precisely what makes Brauer–Siegel on F enough to finish, and the squared form gives back only the trivial exponent. I checked the printed passage again in the 18 February 2017 author copy (§4, p. 6, sha256 bba54fd02aadec75b51f2cdbb312c702c06f44384e45a7ec57832704e4e106ec) and in arXiv v1 (sha256 99ee35275ecb42c52cd8bbc615538dbe6094326fb72894e88ef82c0b89286871); it reads the same in both, and neither gives a citation for it. No claim is made that the printed bound is false — only that it is asserted without proof and does not follow from what genus theory provides. The replacement recovers the theorem: taking Klüners–Wang in a strong induction on the degree, with D_F² ≤ D_K, gives exponent 1/2 - 1/n + O(η) for n = 2m ≥ 6 and D_K^ε for n = 4, both stronger than the 1/2 - 1/(2n) + ε that Theorem 1.1 asserts, so the theorem stands and 'the proof' is the right reach.

sourceIssues.reason: For f_N=x^3-N^2*x, K=Q^3, |Disc(K)|=h_2(K)=1, whereas the 2-Selmer dimensions of E_N:y^2=x^3-N^2*x are unbounded. This contradicts Theorem 1.3(a) and the preceding Selmer estimate. It invalidates the offered deduction of (b), but does not show (b) false: Selmer growth can come from Sha[2].

sourceIssues.reason: Sedunova's cited v1 Theorem 1 contains an epsilon-loss. The published Acta Arithmetica 181.4 (2017), p.321, also retains epsilon and prints an implied constant depending only on d and epsilon, not q. That printed uniformity cannot hold for the stated full range: on Y=X^2 with I={degree<=2 polynomials}, |I|=q^3 and |S|=q^2, so at epsilon=1/12 the ratio to |I|^(1/2+epsilon) is q^(1/4). Thus q-independent use of the cited bound needs an additional repair or restricted range. Neither this constant issue nor the epsilon endpoint is addressed in BSTTTZ's one-sentence reduction. This supports a gap in that deduction, not falsity of the desired torsion bound.
